about: Lismore Castle Gardens round 2, run out of time box after Gort and Doneraile gave one tree. Garden is paid (price not on the arts page; season 13 Mar to 25 Oct 2026, 11-18h, so closed now) and no source names an individual tree; the feature is the yew avenue.

leads.name: Yew avenue, lower garden
leads.source: https://www.ancient-yew.org/yew_trees/lismore-castle-2910/ (Tree Register: avenue planted 1707, avg girth 2.7 m, 16 m, 2009; larger yews thought to grow in less accessible places) + https://lismorecastlearts.ie/plan-your-visit/the-gardens ('much older than the garden itself')
leads.reason: Avenue, ages in popular sources conflict (300, 400, 800 years); one trunk would have to be named. Register row 589 (yew 300-500, 52.13849,-7.93111) is the only individual candidate, unnamed.

leads.source: Heritage Trees of Ireland, Tree Council of Ireland / Aubrey Fennell (NBDC dataset 27, CC BY 4.0), survey 2009
leads.reason: Landmark tree, register only, inside paid castle grounds, no life evidence.

blocked.name: Yew avenue as a whole
blocked.reason: Avenue behind paid entry; one collectible point not established.
